items.t: Entering Georgia in 2026: visa-free stay, insurance, passport
items.d: Visa-free stay, the mandatory health insurance from 2026 and other entry basics for foreign visitors to Georgia.
items.k: Georgia Georgia Since 1 January 2026 every foreign tourist entering Georgia must hold health and accident insurance of at least 30,000 GEL that covers the whole stay. Citizens of 96 countries, including the EU, the USA, the UK, Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan, need no visa and may stay up to one full year. This is the situation as of October 2026.

items.t: Georgia in Winter: Weather, Skiing, Kazbegi and What to See
items.d: What winter in Georgia is like, where to ski, how to visit Kazbegi in snow and what to know about mountain roads.
items.k: Georgia Georgia Winter in Georgia is mild in the lowlands: Tbilisi's average January high is about 6-7 °C, and Batumi's January average is about 5 °C. The mountains get plenty of snow, and ski resorts such as Gudauri, Bakuriani, Mestia and Goderdzi usually run from late December to April. Cities, museums and wine regions stay open all winter.

items.t: Georgia with Kids: Where to Go and Practical Tips for Families

items.k: Georgia Georgia Children usually love Sataplia with its dinosaur footprints, Prometheus Cave, the Batumi Botanical Garden and the sea, Borjomi park and Bakuriani. Choose tours with short walks, pack water, snacks and a warm layer, and remember that mountain day tours take the whole day.

items.t: Best Time to Visit Georgia: Seasons and Months Explained
items.d: Which month suits what: the sea, the mountains, the grape harvest, skiing and sightseeing.
items.k: Georgia Georgia For sightseeing and cities, the best times are late spring (May-June) and autumn (September-October). For the sea and the high mountains, choose July and August. The grape harvest (Rtveli) starts in Kakheti in September, and skiing usually runs from late December to April.

items.t: Truso Valley Day Trip from Tbilisi: Travertines, Ketrisi, Zakagori
items.d: What you see in the Truso valley, how far you walk and how to get ready for a day in the mountains.
items.k: Georgia Georgia Our Truso tour leaves Tbilisi at 07:00 and is back at about 22:00. In the valley you walk 6-7 km one way on an easy path. On the way you see colourful travertines, the 'bottomless' lake, Ketrisi village, Abano Convent and Zakagori Fortress.

items.t: David Gareja and the Colourful Mountains: What to See and Bring
items.d: What you see at David Gareja and the colourful mountains, how much walking there is and how to handle the desert heat.
items.k: Georgia Georgia David Gareja is a rock-cut monastery complex founded in the 6th century, about 60-70 km southeast of Tbilisi in semi-desert. Our colourful desert tour combines the monasteries with the Mravaltskaro colourful mountains, with only about 1 km of easy walking in total. Summers here are very hot, so bring water, a hat and sunscreen.

items.t: Kakheti Day Trips from Tbilisi: Four Routes and Who Each Suits
items.d: Our four Kakheti day routes from Tbilisi: what each one covers and how to choose.
items.k: Georgia Georgia We run four Kakheti day routes: Sighnaghi and Bodbe; Ujarma to Alaverdi; Nekresi, Gremi and Telavi; and Gurjaani and Zegaani. Sighnaghi and Bodbe is best for a first visit, the Alaverdi route for monastery lovers, Gremi and Telavi for history fans, and Gurjaani and Zegaani for people who have already seen the classic sights.

items.t: Before You Travel: What Not to Forget Before Leaving Home
items.d: What to sort out before you leave home: documents, insurance, bank, mobile data, the flight, your home and emergency numbers.
items.k: Greece Greece France France Egypt Egypt Turkey Turkey Sri Lanka Sri Lanka One or two weeks before departure, check your passport's validity and the entry rules, read your insurance policy, tell your bank you're travelling and sort out mobile data. In the last few days, make copies of your documents, download offline maps, check in for your flight and save emergency numbers, including the Consular Department hotline of Georgia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

items.t: Hand Luggage on Low-Cost Flights from Kutaisi: What Fits and What Doesn't
items.d: How to pack 10 kg of hand luggage for a flight from Kutaisi: size, liquids, power banks and items you can't take.
items.k: Italy Italy France France Spain Spain Greece Greece Malta Malta Most of our Kutaisi tours include one piece of hand luggage: 10 kg, 40x30x20 cm. That's the size of a small backpack, not a cabin trolley. Pack liquids in containers of up to 100 ml in one clear 1-litre bag, and keep your power bank in your hand luggage or on you.

items.t: Money Abroad: Card or Cash, Currency, ATMs and Extra Costs
items.d: How to pay abroad: card and cash, exchanging money, ATMs, keeping money safe and budgeting for optional extras.
items.k: Turkey Turkey Spain Spain Portugal Portugal France France Italy Italy Egypt Egypt Take both: a card for hotels, shops and restaurants, and cash for small costs, markets and tips. Take euros for Europe and US dollars for our Egypt tours, where the visa and optional excursions are priced in dollars. Before you go, check your card's terms with your bank, and budget for optional excursions and museums in advance.

items.t: Jordan Visa for Georgian Citizens: On Arrival and Jordan Pass (2026)
items.d: Jordan visa for Georgian passport holders: visa on arrival, the Jordan Pass and the Aqaba port rules.
items.k: Jordan Jordan Egypt Egypt Georgian citizens need a visa for Jordan, but usually do not have to get it in advance: Georgia is not on the Jordanian Ministry of Interior's list of 'restricted' nationalities, so you get the visa on arrival at Amman airport. A single-entry visa costs 40 Jordanian dinars, and Jordan Pass holders who stay at least two nights pay no visa fee (as of October 2026).

items.t: Morocco Visa for Georgian Citizens: eVisa or Embassy Visa (2026)
items.d: Morocco visa for Georgian passport holders: when the eVisa is possible and when you need a consulate.
items.k: Morocco Morocco Yes, Georgian citizens need a visa for Morocco. According to Morocco's official portal (acces-maroc.ma), a Georgian can get an eVisa only if they hold a valid multiple-entry visa from the Schengen area, the USA, the UK or another listed country; otherwise the visa is issued through an embassy or consulate. The Morocco visa is included in the price of our Morocco tour.

items.t: India Visa for Georgian Citizens: e-Visa Types, Fees and Timing (2026)
items.d: India e-Visa for Georgian passport holders: types, the official fee, timing and documents.
items.k: India India Georgian citizens need a visa for India, but they can get it online: Georgia is on the list of countries eligible for India's official e-Visa. As of October 2026 the 30-day e-Tourist Visa costs 25 USD from July to March and 10 USD from April to June, and the 1-year one 40 USD. Apply at least 4 days before you arrive.

items.t: China Visa for Georgian Citizens: Visa-Free Rules and Hong Kong (2026)
items.d: China and Hong Kong for Georgian passport holders: the exact visa-free terms and day limits.
items.k: China China No, Georgian citizens do not need a visa for a short trip to China. Since 28 May 2024 a mutual visa exemption agreement for ordinary passport holders has been in force: each stay must not exceed 30 days, and the total must not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period. Hong Kong has its own rules: Georgians can stay there visa-free for up to 30 days (as of October 2026).

items.t: Sri Lanka and Maldives Visa for Georgian Citizens (2026)
items.d: Sri Lanka ETA and Maldives entry rules for Georgian passport holders: fees, timing and documents.
items.k: Sri Lanka Sri Lanka Maldives Maldives Georgian citizens need an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for Sri Lanka, obtained on eta.gov.lk before arrival: a 30-day tourist ETA costs 50 USD in advance, 60 USD on arrival, and is free for children under 12 (as of October 2026). The Maldives grants a tourist visa on arrival free of charge, but you must submit an online Traveller Declaration within 96 hours before you arrive.

items.t: Kazbegi Day Trip from Tbilisi: Route, Drive and What to Wear
items.d: What you see on a Kazbegi day trip, how much walking there is and what to wear in each season.
items.k: Georgia Georgia Our Kazbegi day tour leaves Tbilisi at 07:00 and is back at about 22:00. You see Dariali Monastery, the big and small Gveleti waterfalls, Gergeti Trinity Church and the Gudauri panorama. The longest walk is to the big waterfall: 1.2 km one way, medium difficulty.

items.t: Best Day Trips from Tbilisi: Where to Go and Who Each Suits
items.d: Our one-day routes from Tbilisi, sorted by how much walking they involve and the best season for each.
items.k: Georgia Georgia For little walking, pick Kakheti, the colourful desert or Kazbegi. If you like hiking, pick Truso (6-7 km one way, easy) or Lagodekhi (8.3 km one way, medium). Go to the mountain routes in the warm months. Kakheti and the lowland routes work for most of the year.

items.t: Cappadocia: Best Time to Visit and Hot-Air Balloon Flights
items.d: Best season for Cappadocia, how the balloon flights work, weather cancellations and what to wear.
items.k: Turkey Turkey According to GoTürkiye, Türkiye's official tourism portal, the best time for a balloon ride is spring or autumn, when the weather is milder and more settled. Flights start just before sunrise, depend on the weather and can be cancelled. On our tour the flight is optional and costs 200-250 EUR.

items.t: Keukenhof 2027: When the Tulip Park in the Netherlands Is Open
items.d: Keukenhof 2027 dates, opening hours, tickets and how to plan around the tulip season.
items.k: Netherlands Netherlands Belgium Belgium Germany Germany According to the official site keukenhof.nl, Keukenhof is open from Thursday 18 March to Sunday 9 May 2027, daily from 8:00 to 19:00, with last entry at 18:15. Flowering depends on the weather, so nobody can say in advance exactly which week will be best.

items.t: Group Tour Checklist: Documents and Packing for Travel from Georgia
items.d: Documents and packing list for a group tour abroad, including what children need to leave Georgia.
items.k: Greece Greece Lithuania Lithuania Slovakia Slovakia Belgium Belgium Bring a passport valid for at least 6 months after the trip, travel insurance, cash and a card, an adapter, your medicines and hand luggage that fits low-cost rules (10 kg, 40x30x20 cm on our tours from Kutaisi). Under Georgian law, a child under 16 needs one parent's permission and an adult escort. If the child travels without a parent, bring a notarised consent and confirm the details in advance.

items.t: Egypt Visa for Georgian Citizens: e-Visa, Fee and Passport (2026)
items.d: Egypt e-Visa for Georgian passport holders: the official fee, passport validity and what to carry.
items.k: Egypt Egypt Yes, Georgian citizens need a visa for Egypt. Georgia is on the list of countries whose citizens can get an e-Visa on Egypt's official portal: as of October 2026 a single-entry tourist e-Visa costs 30 USD and a multiple-entry one 65 USD. Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the day you arrive.

items.t: Turkey with a Georgian ID Card: Entry Rules for Georgian Citizens
items.d: Entering Turkey with a Georgian ID card or passport: visa-free days, passport rules and tips for travelling with children.
items.k: Turkey Turkey Yes. According to Türkiye's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Georgia is on the list of countries whose citizens can enter Türkiye with their national ID card. Georgian citizens do not need a visa for trips of up to 90 days (as of October 2026). A child needs their own valid document.

items.t: Entering Armenia from Georgia: ID Card or Passport?
items.d: Entering Armenia from Georgia: a biometric ID card or a passport, no visa needed.
items.k: Armenia Armenia Georgian citizens do not need a visa for Armenia. Under an agreement in force since 2023, you can enter Armenia with a biometric ID card through an international border checkpoint, or with your passport. Armenia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says visa-free foreigners may stay no more than 180 days in a year, unless an international agreement sets a different term.

items.t: Schengen Without a Visa for Georgians: 90/180, Documents, ETIAS
items.d: Visa-free travel to the Schengen area: the 90/180 rule, documents at the border and ETIAS status in October 2026.
items.k: Italy Italy France France Spain Spain Greece Greece Netherlands Netherlands Germany Germany Georgian citizens with an ordinary biometric passport do not need a visa for short stays in the Schengen area: up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Since March 2026 the visa exemption has been suspended only for diplomatic, service and official passports. As of October 2026 ETIAS is not yet in operation and no start date has been announced.
